item.title: Kansas City invented the crime of jaywalking — and then repealed it
item.description: Kansas City was one of many U.S. cities with laws against jaywalking until advocates realized that police were mostly handing out tickets to Black men. Here's how Kansas City repealed its ban and reclaimed the right to jaywalk.

item.title: Electricity costs are rising fast in Missouri. Is there a fix?
item.description: Electricity prices are increasing and are now the fastest driver of inflation. Plus: Some lawmakers want to break up Missouri’s electric monopolies, but it's unclear if that could lower monthly bills.

item.title: Kansas City Super Bowl rally shooter pleads to lesser charge and gets 2-year sentence
item.description: The family of Lisa Lopez-Galvan, the 43-year-old mother who was killed during the February 2024 mass shooting, said accountability matters, but it won’t bring their loved one back. The Jackson County prosecutor said she could not prove beyond a reasonable doubt that Dominic Miller, 20, was the initial aggressor.

item.title: Gas prices in Kansas and Missouri are among nation's lowest as they spike amid Iran war
item.description: Gas prices average $2.92 in Kansas and $2.98 in Missouri. California tops the nation at $5.20 per gallon.

item.title: Not letting medical debt cut kids from the team
item.description: Sometimes, after an accident, medical bills force families to give up nonessential expenses, like their kids’ sports. A local charity is helping families in that situation. We'll hear from the organization’s founder and families the group has helped.

item.title: Missouri's 'Stand Your Ground' law ended Super Bowl parade murder case, prosecutor says
item.description: Jackson County Prosecutor Melesa Johnson said she got accountability in the case against the 20-year-old involved in the fatal mass shooting. But Johnson vowed to change the law, saying the victim’s family deserved “way more than the law currently allows us to give them.”

item.title: Missouri man said DNA test could prove his innocence. He was executed before a court ruled
item.description: Lance Shockley died by lethal injection last year. State courts have rejected prisoners' requests for DNA testing in recent years.

item.title: Leavenworth opens its doors to ICE detention center
item.description: The Leavenworth City Commission voted to grant CoreCivic a special use permit to operate an ICE detention center, which will be central to President Donald Trump's mass deportation efforts. The vote came despite intense community opposition and a yearlong legal battle.

item.title: Why these Kansas students walked out of school to protest ICE
item.description: Kansas lawmakers are considering restricting student protests after high schoolers organized walkouts across the state in protest of immigration enforcement. We’ll hear from three students about their experience. Plus: We'll go inside the Greenhouse Print Space, a Kansas City studio keeping hundreds of years of printmaking technology alive.

item.title: Former Missouri cop gets 2 years in prison for stealing intimate photos during traffic stops
item.description: Ex-Florissant officer Julian Alcala admitted that he pulled over victims for minor traffic violations, then searched through their phones and sent intimate photos and videos to his own phone.
